properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-20: *"we probably need to pause slightly and do some honest research into what is 'systems engineering and how is reflow2 helping a user do SE?'. I feel like one of the core things we talk about is that reflow2 does SE - so we need to properly back that statement up."* Plus the standard he wants avoided: *"do what I say (those using reflow2), not what I do."*

SEARCHED FIRST. `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` and `req:a-user-can-see-that-the-process-was-followed` already hold his 2026-08-16 version of this and settle two things that are NOT re-litigated here: reflow2 is not a bare vocabulary (genesis and adopt both sequence function before structure and adopt forbids inferring a requirement from its implementation), and THE GAP IS EVIDENCE, NOT GUIDANCE.

⭐ WHAT IS NEW HERE: every prior node reasons from reflow2 OUTWARD. Nobody had taken a recognised definition of systems engineering and audited reflow2 AGAINST it. This is that audit, first pass.

⚠️ METHOD AND ITS BOUND, stated so the audit is not over-trusted: the yardstick is ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288's process framework as published in secondary sources (SEBoK, IEEE/ISO abstracts) — 14 technical processes and 8 technical-management processes. THE STANDARD ITSELF IS PAYWALLED AND WAS NOT READ. Process NAMES and groupings are reliable; any claim about what a specific clause REQUIRES is not made here.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📊 THE AUDIT — vocabulary / tool / CHECK, which is the three-legs test applied to SE itself

TECHNICAL PROCESSES
  Business or Mission Analysis      Project, project mode, genesis brief          check: partial
  Stakeholder Needs & Requirements  Actor, Contributor, Requirement provenance    check: YES
  System Requirements Definition    Requirement, Constraint, KPP, designation     check: YES
  Architecture Definition           Component, level, CONTAINS, Interface,        check: THIN — the
                                    PROVIDES/CONSUMES, ALLOCATED_TO, Flow         hole found 2026-08-20
  Design Definition                 Artifact, REALIZES, SPECIFIES                 check: YES
  System Analysis                   allocation, propagation, budget, ility,       check: YES — STRONGEST
                                    readiness TRL/MRL, alternatives, granularity
  Implementation                    out of scope by design; artifacts + checksums check: n/a
  Integration                       seam_report, compose, mirror, pair_designs    check: YES
  Verification                      Verification, VERIFIES, 8 methods, coverage   check: YES
  Transition                        Release, INCLUDES, deploy_to, Environment     check: partial
  Validation                        Verification.kind = validation                check: YES (unvalidated_capability)
  Operation                         fielded, Environment, performed_in            check: partial
  Maintenance                       ChangeEvent, DriftEvent, dispositions         check: YES
  Disposal                          OBSOLETES, discontinued, retire-from-design   check: YES

TECHNICAL MANAGEMENT PROCESSES
  Project Planning                  plan_epoch, schedule_for, budget, increments  check: partial
  Assessment and Control            loop_status, graph_report, readiness          check: YES
  Decision Management               Decision, alternatives, collapse_decision     check: YES — exceptional
  Risk Management                   🛑 NO NODE TYPE. RISKS/MITIGATES edges only    check: NONE
  Configuration Management          Snapshot, Anchor, Epoch, checksums, lineage   check: YES — exceptional
  Information Management            the graph itself                              check: n/a
  Measurement                       DimensionObservation/Assessment               check: YES
  Quality Assurance                 QualityGate, gate_on, DesignRule enforced     check: partial

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ WHAT THE AUDIT SAYS IN REFLOW2'S FAVOUR, and it is more than expected

The VERIFICATION/VALIDATION SPLIT is modelled correctly and most tools blur it: `Verification.kind` is an enum of exactly {verification, validation} — *"built right (meets the spec)"* versus *"right thing (meets the operational intent/need)"* — on a separate axis from `method`, which carries the four canonical DoD/INCOSE methods (test, analysis, inspection, demonstration) plus `observation` for as-fielded. There is a detector reading it (`unvalidated_capability`). That is real SE fidelity, not vocabulary cosplay.

CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT and DECISION MANAGEMENT are genuinely strong — snapshots, epochs, content-hash lineage, an export chain that refuses to sever itself, and decisions that land `proposed` until a named person's word.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE SELF-HOST ANSWER, MEASURED 2026-08-20 — THIS IS THE "WHAT I DO" HALF

  175 Verifications in reflow2's own graph
  175 are kind = verification
    0 are kind = validation
  168 of 175 use method = test

reflow2 SHIPS the built-right/right-thing distinction, ships a detector for it, and HAS NEVER ONCE USED IT ON ITSELF. Every check it holds asks whether the code matches the spec. Not one asks whether a capability meets an operational need.

And the rest of the vocabulary is used about as thinly:
   1 Constraint          (hard limits: built, essentially unused)
   1 RISKS/MITIGATES edge (risk: no node type, and the edges are unused too)
   3 Actors              (stakeholders)
  42 of 56 Components carry no Interface
   0 of 8 subsystems provide anything
   1 capability-to-capability dependency across 182 allocated capabilities

⚠️ THE FAIR READING, because the prior node already established it: reflow2 has NO genesis epoch and was NEVER taken through adopt. Its graph records organic growth with good bookkeeping, not a guided design. So this is not evidence that the guided path fails — it is evidence that THE TOOL'S OWN DESIGN WAS NOT BUILT BY THE PROCESS THE TOOL SELLS, which is precisely the exposure Anthony named.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ THE HONEST SENTENCE, offered to replace "reflow2 does SE"

**reflow2 supplies a broad and unusually faithful SE vocabulary, enforces a real function-before-structure process on its guided paths, computes system analyses that few tools compute — and enforces very little of it. Its detectors check the CONSISTENCY OF WHAT EXISTS; almost nothing notices what was never done.**

That sentence is defensible, and "reflow2 does SE" unqualified is not.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS

**A. A RISK NODE TYPE.** The one named 15288 process with no vocabulary at all. SE practice runs on a risk register — likelihood, consequence, owner, mitigation, burn-down — and reflow2 has an edge with a severity property and nowhere to put any of it. ⚠️ Counter: `dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them` set the precedent that a domain waits for a project that needs it, and no user has asked for risk.

**B. RUN ADOPT ON REFLOW2 ITSELF.** Already recorded as `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test`. It is the only way to answer "does the guided path work" with evidence rather than testimony, and it would close the do-as-I-do gap directly.

**C. VALIDATE SOMETHING.** Zero of 175. Even a handful of `kind: validation` checks against operational intent would move reflow2 from self-consistent to self-validated — and would exercise a detector nobody has ever seen fire.

**D. A PROCESS-CONFORMANCE REPORT** — option (c) of the prior decision, now with a yardstick: report which 15288 processes this design has evidence for. ⚠️ Counter, and it is `dec:mosa-conformance`'s: a standard's vocabulary belongs in a VIEW, never in the schema, or a design-anything tool takes on one discipline's language.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any user's project uses the vocabulary more completely than reflow2's own does. That comparison would say whether this is a self-host problem or a product one, and nobody has run it.
properties.name: OPEN — the claim "reflow2 does SE" audited against ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 for the first time: broad vocabulary, real process on the guided paths, thin enforcement, and a self-host that uses about a third of what it offers
